                     FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

     COMMENTS OF AMERICAN ELECTRIC POWER SERVICE CORPORATION

        American Electric Power Service Corporation (“AEP”), on behalf of its affiliates,1 submits

the following comments in support of the Study Agreement in Furtherance of the State of Ohio’s

State Agreement Approach Request (“Study Agreement”), submitted on October 13, 2026 by PJM

Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”).2 PJM’s proposal represents the first in a set of components to a

collaborative, innovative public-private partnership and effort to support the reliable provision of

service to a project that is mission-critical to achieving the country’s artificial intelligence goals.

The Study Agreement furthermore provides for a technically sound study methodology that will

allow PJM to efficiently identify, using its established planning processes, the transmission

facilities necessary to reliably serve the incoming large load, and that advances the large load

objectives of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or “the Commission”).

I.      BACKGROUND

        A.      The Flagship Project

         The Flagship Project is a single, integrated development that pairs an artificial intelligence

data center with dedicated generation and transmission infrastructure sited on and near the former

U.S. Department of Energy (“DOE”) Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant in Pike County, Ohio

 (“Piketon Site”). DOE and SE DC DevCo, LLC (with its affiliates PORTS 2 Interconnect, LLC

and Portsmouth Gas DevCo, LLC, “SB Energy”) are collaborating to develop an approximately

10,370 MW artificial intelligence data center (“the Flagship Data Center”) at and around the

Piketon Site. The Flagship Data Center will receive retail service from Ohio Power Company

(“AEP Ohio”) and a competitive retail energy supplier.             SB Energy will also develop

approximately 10,170 MW of new energy generation resources to serve the Flagship Data Center

(“Flagship Generation Portfolio”). As described in more detail below, SB Energy has committed

to financially support the construction of the transmission facilities needed to support the Flagship

Project.

       B.      Anticipated Use of the State Agreement Approach

       Section 1.5.9 of PJM’s Operating Agreement provides the requirements that govern the

State Agreement Approach, which allows state governmental authorities authorized by their

respective states to volunteer responsibility for the allocation of costs of a proposed transmission

expansion or enhancement addressing that state’s public policy requirements.3 On June 15, 2026,

the Ohio Federal Energy Advocate, an office within the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio

(“PUCO”), sent PJM a letter requesting use of the State Agreement Approach process to develop

transmission facilities in furtherance of its Public Policy Requirements set forth in Ohio Revised

Code Section 4928.02, which establishes the State’s public policy for the electric industry to

promote reliable and reasonably priced electric service, competitive electricity markets, consumer

protection, grid modernization, innovation, and economic development.4

       Understanding the significant customer cost implications of the Flagship Project, SB

Energy has committed to ensuring that the costs caused by the Flagship Project are borne by SB

 Energy rather than other customers, and to making a significant investment in the community

surrounding the Piketon Site. SB Energy’s commitment to pay for the infrastructure necessary to

support the Flagship Data Center, as well as its commitment to build the Flagship Generation

Portfolio, demonstrates its adoption of and adherence to the Trump Administration’s Ratepayer

Protection Pledge, pursuant to which data center developers and hyper-scalers have agreed to

protect American consumers from increased electricity costs due to the cost of the energy and

infrastructure required to serve data centers, to build the generation resources needed to satisfy

data center demands, and to invest in local job creation and local development.5

        The specific terms governing the allocation of Flagship Project costs to SB Energy are

anticipated to be contained in a State Agreement Approach Agreement among PJM, the PUCO,

AEP Ohio, AEP Ohio Transmission Company, Inc. (“AEP Ohio Transco”6), and SB Energy

(“Flagship Project SAA”), to be filed with the Commission upon its approval by the PUCO. As

part of the PUCO’s approval of a Flagship Project SAA, the PUCO would agree, pursuant to the

State Agreement Approach process, for the State of Ohio to be responsible for the costs of the

transmission upgrades required to serve the Flagship Project, so that the costs can be assigned to

appropriate affiliates of SB Energy. Any such commitment from the PUCO would be predicated

on SB Energy’s willingness to bear the costs of the Flagship Project.

        AEP Ohio Transco, pursuant to its own reliability studies, has determined that delivering

reliable service to the Flagship Data Center will require the construction of three new 765 kV

transmission lines, substations, and related infrastructure. As described below, the PJM Study will

support AEP Ohio’s and SB Energy’s anticipated use of the State Agreement Approach by

        C.       PJM Study

        In furtherance of the State Agreement Approach process, PJM, SB Energy, and AEP Ohio

Transco have entered into the Study Agreement, pursuant to which PJM will conduct studies to

evaluate the transmission facilities necessary to accommodate the Flagship Project (“PJM Study”).

Specifically, the purpose of the PJM Study is to identify whether any additional transmission

facilities are needed to safely and reliably provide the requested level of Regional Network

Integration Transmission Service (“NITS”) to the Flagship Data Center and the requested level of

Capacity Interconnection Rights (“CIRs”) to the Flagship Generation Portfolio, where such

transmission infrastructure may be located on the systems of AEP Ohio, AEP Ohio Transco,

another PJM Transmission Owner, or an Affected System.7

        Pursuant to the Study Agreement, PJM proposes to conduct an integrated, holistic technical

evaluation of the Flagship Project’s proposed load, generation, and transmission elements.8 PJM’s

evaluation will test the Flagship Project facilities under the operating conditions relevant to the

requested service, including the most credible stressed scenarios, in conformance with PJM

planning standards and all applicable reliability and planning criteria.9

 II.     COMMENTS IN SUPPORT OF THE STUDY AGREEMENT

        AEP has been partnering with SB Energy and PJM for many months to facilitate

development of the Flagship Project. AEP is a signatory to the Study Agreement and strongly

supports its acceptance. The Study Agreement is consistent with the approach PJM has previously

used to implement the State Agreement Approach, including the State Agreement Approach Study

Agreement submitted by PJM in Docket No. ER21-689-000.10 As in that proceeding, the Study

Agreement provides for PJM to conduct a study, using its established planning tools and criteria,

of the transmission enhancements needed to support a state public policy requirement.

        The Flagship Project comprises the Flagship Data Center, the Flagship Generation

Portfolio, and the AEP Ohio Transco-identified 765 kV transmission upgrades, as well as

associated transmission facilities. The Study Agreement accordingly provides a single analytical

framework for PJM to evaluate the requested level of NITS for the Flagship Data Center and the

requested level of CIRs for the Flagship Generation Portfolio.11 This is a practical, technically

sound approach to addressing the request from the Ohio Federal Energy Advocate that leverages

PJM’s existing processes for assessing system reliability while ensuring that the transmission

solution identified reflects how the system will operate once all components of the Flagship Project

are in service, including under the most credible stressed scenarios.

        The Study Agreement is aligned with the direction of the Commission’s ongoing efforts to

address the challenges associated with the integration of large loads, including the need for clear

and consistent procedures for studying the provision of transmission service to large loads.12 In

ER24-1187-000 (Apr. 1, 2024) (accepting SAA study agreement).

 the June 2026 Show Cause Order, the Commission identified the need for study procedures that

account for the unique characteristics and impacts of large loads, including procedures that identify

the transmission facilities necessary to reliably accommodate new large loads.13 The Study

Agreement advances these objectives by providing a coordinated evaluation of the Flagship

Project that is tailored to the project’s integrated nature and will identify the facilities necessary to

maintain system reliability.

        Under the Study Agreement, PJM will apply to studying the Flagship Project the same

technical rigor it applies to all requested services. PJM’s analysis will be grounded in the same

substantive reliability requirements that govern its other planning and interconnection studies,

including load-flow, short-circuit, and stability analyses applying the applicable NERC Reliability

Standards, PJM reliability criteria, and individual Transmission Owner planning criteria.14 The

Flagship Project will therefore be held to the same reliability benchmarks as any other load or

generation seeking service on the PJM system, and the Study Agreement provides an efficient path

for PJM to identify the facilities needed to reliably serve the Flagship Data Center on a timeframe

consistent with the Flagship Project’s development schedule and in a manner consistent with the

Ohio Federal Energy Advocate’s request.

        In addition to recognizing the need for large load study procedures, the June 2026 Show

Cause Order recognized that the integration of large loads “implicate[s] both federal and state

interests” and “will require the involvement of both federal and state actors.”15 The Study

Agreement, if accepted, will establish a common technical foundation that will inform SB

Energy’s and the PUCO’s consideration of whether to proceed under the State Agreement

 Approach. By doing so, the Study Agreement acts as the first in a set of coordinated steps toward

obtaining the state- and federal-level approvals necessary to implement the Flagship Project.

       Commission acceptance of the Study Agreement does not pre-judge any future

Commission action on filings related to the State Agreement Approach. The Study Agreement is

limited to PJM’s assessment of the incremental transmission facilities necessary to reliably serve

the Flagship Project. Neither the Study Agreement nor the PJM Study results authorize the

construction of any facilities necessary to implement the Flagship Project, designate entities to

construct such facilities, establish cost allocations, or grant any interconnection rights.16 All such

matters will be the subject of subsequent filings before the Commission.

 III.   CONCLUSION

       WHEREFORE, for the foregoing reasons, AEP respectfully requests that the

Commission accept the Study Agreement.
